description: Research in this topic addresses the structures and processes of crime and criminal justice, from crime detection to incarceration and rehabilitation. Case studies focused on methods for identifying and preventing crime, with particular emphasis on emerging online threats. They improved efficacy of crime prevention and policing, informing police ethics, job satisfaction and community collaboration. Research informed victim support, and shaped policy and reform in the judicial system to promote fairness and efficiency. Studies also addressed prison life, deepening understanding and supporting rehabilitation, guiding policies to foster reintegration and reduce reoffending.

Case studies in this topic preserved, recorded/recorded, reinterpreted and promoted musical heritage across historical and global contexts, while pioneering new technologies in sound design, audio curation and immersive experiences. Research celebrates diverse musical traditions, building cross-cultural engagement and understanding. It also advances inclusive music-making, performance and listening experiences. Projects supported therapeutic uses of music, expanding access through innovative technological and curational practices, and enhanced music education, improving cultural understanding and creative participation.

Case studies in this topic focus on waste management and recycling. Studies tend to consider the environmental and health impacts of waste through innovations in policy, materials, and industrial practice. They include advances in waste management across areas such as plastic, food waste, and electronic waste, alongside circular economy initiatives like carbon-negative building materials and sustainable cosmetics. The research has influenced legislation, developed British Standards, improved public understanding, and fostered commercial success in transforming waste into valuable resources.

Case studies in this topic addressed the commemoration and public understanding of military history by augmenting engagement with historic events, communities and individuals. Case studies developed archival records and increased accessibility though digitisation and public engagement and educational opportunities. Work engaged highlighted the ongoing relevance of historical events, shaping contemporary perceptions of certain events or experiences and informing reconciliation efforts. A key focus was on elevating the narratives of minority or marginalised communities and voices, and developing inclusive approaches to remembrance.

Research in this topic encourages participation in the arts and heritage for wellbeing, education and community cohesion. Case studies used innovate curatorial and creative practices to bring artistic and historical culture to the public in new forms and settings, fostering inclusivity, co-creation and meaningful dialogue. Many engaged with underrepresented voices or histories to affirm identity, strengthen community ties and influence cultural policy. Many had lasting social and economic benefits for local areas, enhancing the visibility and value of arts and heritage in public life.

Research in this topic informs the protection of cultural property and safeguarding of heritage and related community identities. Case studies influence foreign policy, reconciliation efforts and peacebuilding through the protection of cultural assets and promotion of heritage rights. Many projects used digitisation and novel archival techniques to preserve at-risk heritage and improve accessibility. Research also informed conservation in the context of areas of modernisation and regeneration, preserving cultural heritage while serving the needs of communities and infrastructure. International collaboration and innovative technologies and curatorial practices underpinned sustainable conservation. A strong emphasis is on increasing public access and engagement, enhancing the appreciation, resilience and global visibility of cultural heritage.

Research in this topic focuses on the preservation, protection and engagement with archaeology, material heritage and historic sites. Case studies inform policy and protection efforts, while new research methods and technologies expand archaeological discovery and curatorial and exhibition practices. Projects enhanced accessibility and visitor experiences through creative staging, performance and digital tools. Educational incentives deepened connections to cultural heritage and identity, fostering cross-cultural understanding and informing local and national narratives. Many projects also generated significant social and economic benefits for heritage sites and their communities.

This topic addresses science outreach, communication and education. Case studies in this topic discuss how public understanding may be broadened through participation and access to exhibitions, outreach events, digital platforms, and media. It demonstrates increased engagement with science, for example in astronomy, quantum biology, particle physics, ethics, and evolution, often using creative formats such as museums, storytelling, and art–science collaborations. Studies in this topic also address improvements to education and have impacts in educational resources and curricula, enhancing schooling and improving equality in participation in STEM education and science communication.

Research in this topic supports and informs business, entrepreneurialism, management and policies aimed at improving the founding and productivity of commercial enterprisees. Much research focuses on identifying and implementing effective tools for managing existing firms and means to make entrepreneurs successful. This includes both practices and training inside firms as well as the development of business or entrepreneurialism-friendly policies and funding. We also find several business spinoffs from research or adaptations of research into large companies. A large number of impact projects are concerned with helping small- and medium enterprises (SMEs) grow and with creating business environments, organisational practices, public policies and financial opportunities that help them thrive. Research on management reguarly informs ways to make firms more efficient and to train their staff. Several projects are also concerned with environmental and sustainable practices in business and entrepreneurialism for a greener economy.

Research in this topic enhances care for the elderly and those living with age-related conditions such as dementia, Alzheimer’s and Parkinson’s disease. Case studies shaped healthcare policy and practice through innovations in early detection, practitioner training and assistive technologies. They addressed social care aspects, many involving families and communities to raise awareness and deliver social initiatives that support independent living, reduce loneliness and promote inclusion, with a key focus on changing perceptions of the elderly and their needs. A key focus in on shifting public understanding of ageing and encouraging lifelong habits and early intervention strategies that support healthy ageing and improved quality of life.

This topic covers vision research and opthamology. In general studies in this topic demonstrate research into understanding, diagnosing, preventing, treating and supporting those with vision-threatening conditions. The topic features therapy and treament innovations as well as care and support initiatives for those affected. Research across this topic has enhanced visual care for patients, informed international guidelines, advanced identification and management of optical conditions and been commercialised. Across clinical, community, and global settings, the studies often reflect better service delivery, public health strategies, and increased quality of life for people with visual impairments.

The research in this topic addresses reproductive, maternal, and neonatal health. Law, policy and guidance are informed by studies addressing clinical practice, access and equity, as well as the development of therapies are inlcluded here. Studies researching aspects of childbirth and reproductive health such as contraception and fertility, newborn outcomes, bereavement support, and advancements in pharmacological, psychological, behavioural, and assisted reproductive therapies are all encompassed by this topic.

This topic encompasses research relating to water, flood and coastal management. Studies cover flood risk management and resilience, as well as coastal and marine management, sustainable water systems and infrastructure, environmental water management initiatives as well as water access and equity. Research in this topic is broadly applied, but often showcases technology and methodology for monitoring and detection; modelling, simulation and prediction; treatment and processing; assessment and decision-making; and communication of data to public and professional bodies.

This research topic showcases research across healthcare services, data and policy. It focuses on patient-centred care, digital health innovation, and community engagement for more inclusive, personalised, and effective services. It highlights advances in workforce and organisational transformation, policy influence, and behavioural science to improve both delivery and outcomes. Underpinning these developments are enhanced methods for ensuring safety and clinical quality, supported by rigorous data evaluation and measurement tools.

Research in this topic informs urban planning and transportation policy, advancing the design and implementation of more efficient, inclusive, and resilient mobility systems. Case studies shaped investment strategies and infrastructure priorities, with strong emphasis on accessibility for disabled people, the elderly, and children, as well as supporting active urban lifestyles. Many case studies focus on sustainability, addressing the challenges of climate change and uncertainty through innovative and ecologically responsible planning. Research also extended beyond urban environments to include broader logistical systems such as airport infrastructure, regional transit, and transport ticketing systems. Novel tools and technologies were developed to support planners and transport organisations in overcoming complex mobility and logistics challenges across diverse contexts.

Research in this topic explores the cultural legacy, contemporary practice, and uses of performance across theatre, dance, and related art forms. Case studies span writing, acting, directing, choreography, design, and emerging stage technologies, highlighting the creative breadth of live performance. Work celebrates the rich heritage of British theatre, particularly the enduring impact of Shakespeare, while also exploring a diverse range of dance practices and non-theatrical performance traditions. Many projects promote inclusion and diversity in both production and participation, using performance as a platform for the expression of marginalised voices and cross-cultural discourse, building community relationships and mutual understanding. There is also emphasis on education, with theatre and dance used to engage youth, support performer training, and explore complex historical and social narratives.

Research in this topic focuses on developing responsible information environments by tackling misinformation, enhancing media literacy, and promoting frameworks for impartiality and open communication. Case studies have informed global government, institutional, and corporate communication policies that protect democratic processes and ensure access to trusted information. Work supports educators, media professionals, organisations, and the public in navigating the digital information landscape. It strengthens connections between regulators, broadcasters, institutions, and audiences, shaping both public understanding and communication practices. Research also promoted diversity and representation across journalism, news, and wider media communications.

topic_name_long: Brexit, UK & EU policies, Intl. Trade
description: Research in this topic shaped understanding and responses to Brexit, its legal implications, and the redefinition of the UK’s place in the world. Case studies informed the redrawing of UK legislation and legal frameworks, supported the protection of EU nationals’ rights, and guided the restructuring of Britain’s foreign relations. Scholars played a central role in communicating the consequences of Brexit to the public and in advising on the future of UK governance, trade policy, and regulatory structures. Research also supported British Overseas Territories and informed collaboration with Ireland on border and policy issues. Beyond Brexit, work on EU policymaking and trade institutions enhanced understanding of EU-specific rights and shaped evolving trade policy. Broader international trade research addressed global trade rules, WTO processes, and macroeconomic modelling to support more effective and equitable trade negotiations and policy development.

Research in this topic relates to climate change and environmental policy, and studies encompass climate science and modeling, carbon budgets and emissions targets, climate risk assessment, climate communication and public engagement, international climate diplomacy, climate justice and social vulnerability mapping, climate resilience and infrastructure. Research here tends to use modelling and visualisation tools, as well as assessment and data analysis tools to inform policy and organisational decisions.

Research in this topic informed interactions with art, history and science through innovative exhibitions and technologies. Case studies shaped museum and institutional practices, promoting and enabling greater public engagement with both familiar subjects and underrepresented areas in art, heritage and science. Many used exhibitions as platforms for education, cross-cultural understanding and social inclusion, often generating significant social and economic benefits for host communities. Work in this topic highlights the role of cultural engagement in enhancing social and individual wellbeing and inspiring participation of new, diverse audiences.

This topic encompasses case studies relating to energy systems and decarbonisation. Studies address areas such as renewable energy technologies, policy development, building energy efficiency, decarbonization and net-zero transitions, smart energy systems, and socio-economic impacts of energy transitions. Research inlcudes both technical solutions (i.e. smart systems, materials for heat storage, solar photovoltaic monitoring, CO2 capture, AI-integrated systems), and policy tools (i.e. energy mapping, economic modeling, regulatory methodologies, community engagement). The work spans from addressing fuel poverty through targeted neighborhood mapping to supporting large-scale policy development for energy directives and decarbonisation strategies.

The case studies in this topic cover themes in food and agricultural research, with a focus on systems and policy. Studies look at areas such as food security and resilience, sustainable agricultural transformation and practice, food safety and quality systems, and innovation and policy integration. The topic as a whole showcases developing new technologies, financial tools, and governance frameworks to support food and agricultural transformations at local and international levels.

topic_name_long: Pensions, Finances, Consumer Protection and Market Regulation
description: Research in this topic has shaped the regulation of financial services and various goods markets with the goal of protecting consumers and retail investors. Case studies informed policies of key regulatory bodies such as the Financial Conduct Authority and improved various regulations such as oversight of credit cards, payday lending, and complaint handling. Projects enhanced financial literacy and reduced risks linked to gambling, indebtedness, and financial vulnerability. Research drove reforms in insurance and pension practices and regulations, supporting better retirement outcomes and financial security. Contributions also improved market transparency and pricing in housing, pharmaceuticals, and tech products, guided merger and cartel policies, and influenced accounting standards and business regulation to safeguard consumer interests.

Case studies in this topic inform policy, legislation and protective measures for vulnerable workers and groups vulnerable to exploitation, including those affected by modern slavery, human trafficking, illegal sex work and the drug trade. ICSs raise awareness of often unheard or stigmatised experiences, amplifying the voices of marginalised communities to challenge public and institutional perceptions. Work in this topic advocates for more inclusive representation and reforms in national and international legal and policy frameworks to recognise and protect those most affected by exploitative systems.

Research in this topic surrounds the development and utilisation of imaging and assessment techniques for diagnosis, prognosis and monitoring of conditions. Case studies encompass development of sensing and imaging technologies, as well as methods for analysis and use of procured data. Improving accuracy, patient experience and reducing risk are all key elements within the topic.

topic_name_long: Robotics, Sensors, AI, Satellite & Image Data and Smart Systems
description: Research in this topic is applicable to advanced robotics, artificial intelligence, sensor and smart system technologies and image data across a breadth of sectors. Studies encompass autonomous systems for agriculture, manufacturing, and transportation, alongside sophisticated imaging and detection technologies for security, space applications, and industrial monitoring. Case studies demonstrate the commercialisation of AI-powered solutions including computer vision systems, natural language processing tools, and robotic platforms that enhance productivity and safety. The topic aslso includes sensor development for gas detection, structural monitoring, and environmental applications, as well as satellite-based monitoring systems for agricultural and urban planning. Additionally, research covers the integration of these technologies into smart systems that support decision-making, automate complex processes, and enable new capabilities in healthcare, forensics, and public safety applications.

Research in this topic has shaped how cities, towns, and rural areas are planned, built, and governed to promote livability, inclusion, and sustainability. Case studies informed national housing policies, supported legislative reform on housing rights, and influenced regulations on building standards, property valuation, and taxation. Projects helped develop affordable and social housing and gave voice to tenants and community groups in shaping their environments. Providing social and legislative support as well as shelter for the homeless was another major research focus. Research enhanced urban development through virtual city models and spatial planning tools, while also supporting greener cities, accessible public spaces, and integration of diverse populations. In rural areas, research guided strategies to reinvigorate communities and improve local infrastructure and services.

Research in this topic focuses on approaches to viral disease prevention and control. Vaccine development, strategy and policy is an important component of this, at national and global level. Additionally new anti-viral treatments and diagnostics are included, alongside mathematical modeling and data analysis, epidemic response, and some virus-specific research (i.e. genomic studies). There is additionally a contingent of studies with focus on health policy, global health impact and access equity for virus control and vaccine deployment.

This research topic focuses on cancer treatments, support and care for patients. Key themes included are early detection and screening innovations, precision medicine and targeted therapies and treatment technologies. There's a strong emphasis on patient-centered care that prioritises the overall experience and wellbeing of cancer patients. Elements of clinical guidance, policy and service management specific to cancer are also included.

Case studies in this topic contain research surrounding neurological and neuropsychiatric diseases and their management. Studies include development of new treatments, treatment management, assessment, diagnosis and imaging. Furthermore, healthcare services for long-term support and rehabiliation are included, along with clinical practice guidelines and policy specific to this disease area.

Research in this topic investigates malaria and tropical diseases, this includes understanding disease burden and achieving disease control through policy and strategy, awareness and prevention. Modelling of tropical diseases, healthcare access, economics and regulations are all encompassed, as are treatments, drug development and diagnostics. Studies into vector control for malaria and tropical diseases are also inlcuded.

Research in this topic has shaped migration policy, supported migrant integration, and amplified migrant and refugee voices in public life. Projects informed international, national and local policies, improved data on migration flows, and guided service provision for migrant youth and communities. Research supported NGOs, enhanced legal protections, and addressed challenges such as racism, trafficking, and smuggling networks. Following Brexit, studies helped adapt UK migration policy and underpinned public discourse with research based insights. Creative and co-curated initiatives—ranging from arts-based events to faith-led global efforts—helped struggling populations, raised awareness and shared the lived experiences of refugees,migrants and diasporas, fostering empathy, inclusion, and evidence-based engagement.

The case studies in this topic relate to research into cardiovascular health. This covers all aspects of cardiovascular health from treatments and management of conditions, to drug and device development, diagnosis, imaging and monitoring of conditions. It also inludes resarch informing clinical practice guielines, patient safety guidance, screening and prevention, and risk management strategies for patients. Finally, studies into public awareness and action for improved public health are included.

Case studies in this topic are underpinned by global health impacts in healthcare guidance and regulation. This includes reasearch studies into areas such as healthcare policy, access and equity, economics, strategy and resource management. There are also studies into medical developments, such as diagnostics and treaments, healthcare decision making, and clinical practice guidance with globally-reaching impact.

This topic includes case studies pertaining to prostate cancers, including health policy surrounding prostate cancers, as well as treatments and therapies, clinical practise standards, and screening, imaging, diagnostics, prognoses for patients.

topic_name_long: Macroeconomics, Monetary policy, Financial Markets & Banking
description: Research in this topic has strengthened the design, governance, and resilience of financial and monetary systems. Case studies informed central banks—including the Bank of England, ECB, US Federal Reserve, and others globally—on monetary policy and interventions, debt sustainability, bond auction designs and macroprudential policies. Work shaped the toolkit available for responses to financial crises through new bank rescue and stress testing schemes, and systemic risk mitigation strategies. Central Banks were equipped with improved research based tools influencing interest rate decisions, credit risk assessment, and financial market stability. Research also improved more general macroeconomic modelling, forecasting, and official statistics.. Projects also supported regulatory reform in banking and credit sectors. Many mathematical and computational research projects advanced asset and option pricing tools in financial markets. They also informed ESG investment strategies, digital banking innovation, and inclusive practices such as microfinance.

Case studies in this topic focus on educational and therapeutic initiatives and practical provisions that promote literacy and reading practices. Work provides innovative, research-informed approaches to reading comprehension, informing educational policies and supporting adoption of new teaching methods and tools across schools and adult learning settings. Many studies promote public engagement with reading at all stages of life, and underpinned provisions such as funding for public libraries and widening access to reading-related technologies.

This topic focuses on advances in medical treatments and therapies including the development, evaluation, and implementation of treatment options for patients. Studies encompass diagnostics, clinical decision-making, and management strategies that inform treatments and therapies used, as well as the research and development of new treatments. Case studies also often discuss policy and standards of care. The topic includes a broad range of disease areas and treatment types.

Research in this topic has improved the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of infectious diseases and addressed the global challenge of antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Work has shaped international guidelines on antibiotic stewardship, transformed national infection control policies, and reduced antimicrobial use in both human and veterinary medicine. Studies have accelerated drug discovery, including new antibiotic classes and antifungals, and advanced therapies for tuberculosis, Clostridioides difficile, and aspergillosis among others. Researchers have influenced WHO strategies, developed infection-resistant materials and hospital technologies, and improved novel genomic diagnostics. Communication, design, and systems-based interventions have also supported better public and clinical engagement with AMR.

Case studies in this topic raise awareness of disabilities and offer technological and therapeutic innovations to support those living with disabilities across a range of settings. Work informs public education, institutional policy, and practical interventions aimed at changing attitudes and improving social participation for people with disabilities. Many focused on enhancing educational provisions and outcomes for disabled individuals. Work in arts and performance plays a key role in promoting inclusive practices and fostering meaningful connection between disabled and non-disabled communities.

Research in this topic has advanced the design, control and resilience of modern electricity systems, supporting a global shift toward low-carbon and decentralised energy. Innovations have enhanced the efficiency and reliability of power transmission and distribution—particularly in integrating offshore renewables and balancing AC/DC networks. Projects informed smart grid development, demand-side flexibility, and equitable access through minigrids in remote and underserved areas. New modelling and simulation tools have shaped energy infrastructure planning, improved overvoltage protection, and underpinned the UK’s electricity capacity market. Work has also driven international renewable deployment, reduced emissions, and enabled novel technologies for microgeneration, such as microbial fuel cells for off-grid sanitation and lighting.

Research in this topic has transformed organ donation and transplant systems, advanced kidney and liver preservation technologies, and improved treatments for various organ conditions. Work has informed national organ allocation strategies and public health campaigns, with particular impact on reducing inequalities in donor registration. Innovations have enhanced viability and utilisation of donor organs and improved survival outcomes among others in dialysis and nephrotic syndrome care. Genetic insights and precision therapies have shaped guidelines and enabled earlier, more effective interventions for adults and children worldwide.

Case studies in this topic focus on contemporary and historical feminist initiatives for women’s rights and histories. Work informed gender-sensitive reforms in government, legislation, and global politics. ICSs address the protection of women’s rights and celebration of women’s historic and contemporary contributions at local, national and international levels. Work also promotes public education and engagement, fostering deeper understanding of both past and present struggles and achievements in the pursuit of gender equality.

Case studies in this topic used research-informed performance, theatre, and creative arts as tools for therapeutics, health and education. This included drawing on historical and philosophical approaches to mental wellbeing, performance in hospice settings, and somatic arts to aid in patient care and communication as well as supporting practitioner resilience and wellbeing. Work also raises awareness of societal and environmental issues and empowers marginalised voices through innovate forms of expression and creative collaboration. These approaches contribute to cultural understanding and inform policy related to health, wellbeing and social care for specific groups.

This topic centres on research and practice related to neurodevelopmental conditions, such as autism, ADHD, and cerebral palsy. Case studies explore themes such as diagnosis, therapies, and ongoing support; equitable access to services; inclusive education and workplace integration; and policy frameworks promoting patient and carer well-being. Broader considerations include cultural awareness, professional training, and health and social care systems for support of neurodivergent individuals across the lifespan.

Case studies in this topic focus on research and development of advanced physics and chemistry technology with a strong emphasis on real-world application. Studies are broad bringing together enabling technologies (i.e. quantum systems, photonics, semiconductors, electromagnetic, chemical technologies) with application-driven sectors (i.e. maufacturing, analytics, space, catalysis, healthcare, electronics). There’s also a clear through-line of commercial and entrepreneurial focus, connecting early-stage R&D with scalable industry solutions via start-ups, investment, and technology transfer. The breadth of themes within the topic to reflect interdisciplinary integration and real-world impact of the studies.

Case studies in this topic focus on official histories, commemoration practices and the role of historical memory in reconciliation around the second world war. Many worked to document and preserve and the experience of a range of groups, often in collaboration with survivors, local archives, and communities. Particular attention is on contested cultural histories and ‘forgotten’ voices of vulnerable or minority communities in World War II. Emphasis is placed on education and open archives to inform public and institutional understandings, fostering constructive engagement with complex and sensitive histories. This includes German, Russian and Holocaust narratives, and their commemoration and reconciliation for community wellbeing.

Case studies in this topic are concerned with all aspects of teaching and education, shaping policy and approaches to foster better experiences and outcomes for both teachers and learners. They focus on enhancing teaching and education through training educators and developing research-based pedagogical tools and approaches to improve learning outcomes across all education levels, from early years to universities, vocational training and apprenticeships. Case studies shaped curriculum reform and the modernisation of teaching methods, often through integrating technology in the classroom. Emphasis is placed on equity and inclusivity, informing policies and interventions that promote access to education for diverse learners and that support lifelong learning.

Case studies in this topic support the teaching, preservation and revitalisation of languages to reclaim and promote heritage and cultural identities, and to broaden horizons in an increasingly globalised world. Many focused on safeguarding endangered languages and improving access to linguistic resources through digitisation, community collaboration, and public outreach. Work also focused on education and pedagogical approaches to reading and language, promoting foreign language learning and supporting multilingualism. Many trialled innovative approaches, new technologies, and developments in teacher training to enrich language education for teachers, learners, and public worldwide.

Case studies in this topic support a range of initiatives and policies improving the care, wellbeing and legal rights and protection of women, children and families. ICSs span diverse settings, informing childcare services, early childhood interventions, support for children in care and those with disabilities, and strategies to reduce poverty and inequalities. There is strong emphasis on amplifying the voices of children ,young people and adolescents to guide social interventions and policy reform. It also informs education for parents and practitioners, contributing to national and international politics on family care and parental rights. Research also addresses legal and practical support for victims of domestic abuse and sexual violence, shaping public awareness, legislation and institutional responses.

Research in this topic has strengthened democratic institutions and expanded opportunities for citizen engagement. Projects shaped legislation and practice on freedom of information, lobbying transparency, and judicial independence, while seeking ways to improve parliamentary practices in the four nations of the UK, the EU and globally. Research enhanced democratic accountability by supporting electoral participation, public petitions, and citizen assemblies. Digital tools and arts-based initiatives promoted active citizenship and civic inclusion, especially among underrepresented groups. Studies empowered grassroots movements, influenced constitutional reform, and deepened public trust in political processes through more transparent, participatory decision-making.

Case studies in this topic focus on research pertaining to pain management and palliative care, for example considering improvement of policy, of public and professional education, and of service provision for patients. Pain assessment and management are included for a range of patient groups, from chronic to long-term conditions and young patients. End-of-life care and ethics and decision-making for patients is also incorporated in the topic.

Case studies in this topic used novel design and design approaches to improve accessibility and inclusion for diverse and often vulnerable groups, with a particular focus on disabled communities. Research emphasised user-centred design, driving innovation and improving understanding of varied needs across multiple settings, including the creative arts, healthcare and urban environments. Case studies demonstrate how inclusive design can foster greater participation, equity and empowerment through thoughtful, responsive design approaches.

This topic includes case studies focussed on healthcare access and equity. Subject matter includes equity of health service provision, access to healthcare, social care and health information, and to community and social enterprises for health and well-being. Additionally, healthcare systems, policy, funding, investment and spending all feature in this topic with a focus on improving access and equity of healthcare.

Case studies in this topic focus on higher education and universities, their policies, education practices, institutional culture and student experiences. They address issues such as preventing abuse and harassment both online and offline. There is a strong emphasis on inclusivity and widening access for underrepresented groups, promoting equity and improved participation and outcomes. Research also informed curriculum development and pedagogical innovation, such as cross-cultural collaboration and personalised learning support. Research informs policy and practice that enhances the global role of universities and their place in shaping narratives around social mobility, migration, and freedom of information.

Case studies in this topic focus on provisions for sporting environments and opportunities safe from abuse or discrimination and promote the potentials for sport to support wider social and political change. Work highlighted sport’s potential to enhance health, social change, wellbeing and community cohesion at all levels of participation, from grassroots to elite performance. Research advanced coaching strategies and athlete development and achievement, as well as underpinning initiatives to improve the health and wellbeing of athletes and general public alike at all levels of recreational and professional participation. Case studies supported ethical practices in sport, including anti-doping measures and enforcing duties of care held by coaches and institutions, and opened discourse around harmful competitive cultures.

topic_name_long: Children: Care, Development, Education, Rights, Health
description: Research in this topic supported national and international efforts to improve outcomes for children by informing child-focused policies, care systems and educational practices. Case studies underpinned governmental and non-governmental services and policies which address childcare provision, safety, education, wellbeing and legal rights, especially for children in care, with disabilities, or facing poverty. Many worked to centre children’s voices and agency, improving their participation in shaping services that impact their lives. Work also informed safeguarding practices, including protection from abuse and emerging online threats.

The case studies in this topic focus on research around tobacco and smoking, this includes health research into smoke and second-hand smoke impacts, as well as for alternatives (i.e. e-cigarettes). Studies also cover policy and law, marketing ethics and public messaging, generally focussed on reducing usage and the impacts of smoking on public health and wellbeing.

Research in this topic has shaped the technologies, policies, and practices that safeguard digital infrastructure, protect privacy, and combat cybercrime. Projects have informed national and international cybersecurity standards, strengthened industrial and governmental incident response, and guided inclusive, human-centred approaches to digital risk. Work has enabled secure encryption, privacy-preserving computation, and AI-driven cyber threat detection across sectors—from aviation to healthcare. Researchers have improved online safety for children, influenced data protection regulation, and supported digital resilience for small businesses.

This portfolio of research addresses neurodegenerative and genetic diseases, and particularly focuses on therapeutic development and clinical management. The research encompasses treatments and therapies, including drug development, diagnostic services, and improvements to care services, clinical guidelines and policies. It also considers holistic patient care, incorporating case studies on patient and family support for improved quality of life.

Research in this topic has advanced the use of biometric data for security, identity verification, health, and justice. Projects enabled reliable speech and facial recognition, forensic voice and DNA analysis, and the creation of realistic synthetic speech and animation. Innovations have supported refugee identification, border control, and forensic investigations, while also transforming accessibility and communication for people with speech impairments. Work shaped public and commercial use of biometric technologies, influenced policing practice, and guided policy on ethical and algorithmic governance of biometric systems.

Case studies in this topic informed public health policy, physical activity guidelines and education initiatives, supporting long-term behaviour change and improved population health. They promoted physical activity in the general population through the creation of supportive, inclusive environments and improved health education, underpinning efforts to increase participation among underrepresented groups, including women, children and disable individuals. Research also aided the integration of physical activity into healthcare strategies for treatment and prevention, including physiotherapy and post-surgical care to improve patient outcomes, and promoting regular movement to lower the risk of sedentary-lifestyle-related diseases.

Research in this topic has shaped global efforts to prevent, resolve, and recover from violent conflict. Case studies supported peace and reconciliation efforts in regions such as Afghanistan, Syria, and Colombia, informed international diplomacy and post-conflict reconstruction, and guided UK policy towards conflict as well as UN peacekeeping strategies. Projects promoted inclusive peace processes, advancing new global norms and laws to strengthen women’s participation and civil society leadership. Research contributed to transitional justice and reconciliation efforts—from documenting genocide in Rwanda and Indonesia to shaping school curricula and community healing. Partnerships with governments, NGOs, and international agencies are a recurring aspect of research impact in this domain. Researchers also influenced terror prevention and counter-radicalization efforts in the UK. Statistical work improved conflict prediction through data science and created more solid evidence bases for the analysis of violent conflict. Work ranged from high-level political advice for peace processes to very direct practical efforts such as demining post-war landscapes.

Case studies in this topic focus on the production, exhibition, and curation of film and television as a means of preserving heritage, shaping public understanding, and informing societal and political discourse. Case studies celebrate the history and culture of film and cinema, examining its role in commemoration, representation, and reclaiming marginalised or ‘hidden’ histories. A number of studies focus on improving access to film and television archives, enhancing curatorial practices to encourage engagement and preservation. Research also highlights the potential of film for reframing both past and future narratives, foster cross-cultural engagement and inclusive storytelling.

Research in this topic encompasses epidemiology and COVID-19. Case studies span epidemiology from detection, characterisation, monitoring and surveillance of disease, to modelling and public health protection strategies including policy development. Furthermore, studies into specifically COVID-19 are included in this topic, covering areas such as diagnosis, transmission, intervention and treatments, as well as risk management, response, and policy.

Research in this topic has advanced global efforts to protect biodiversity, manage ecosystems sustainably, and align conservation with social justice. Projects informed international frameworks and national policies, guiding the design of biodiversity indicators, invasive species management, and carbon offset strategies. Work amplified Indigenous knowledge, strengthened protected area governance, and developed community-based and participatory conservation models. Studies shaped responses to climate change impacts on ecosystems, enhanced restoration and land-use practices, and improved the integration of conservation with rural livelihoods, resource use, and environmental justice. Research has supported better decision-making tools, novel monitoring technologies, and sustainable practices across forests, wetlands, rangelands, and peatlands globally.

Research in this topic has advanced the decarbonisation of transport through innovations in electric mobility, hydrogen systems, and low-emission propulsion technologies. Projects shaped the development of electric vehicles and batteries, supported the use of alternative fuels, and informed industrial design and strategy. Researchers enabled reductions in carbon and resource intensity by improving motor efficiency, fuel systems, and materials. Work also supported the rollout of hydrogen infrastructure and smart energy integration, influencing national transport and energy policy. Further contributions improved freight logistics and vehicle control systems, supporting a broader transition to sustainable and low-carbon mobility.

Case studies in this topic shaped more effective strategies for self-harm and suicide prevention through improvements in identifying and safeguarding vulnerable individuals in a range of contexts. Case studies inform targeted interventions strategies through improved understanding and regulation of social media and access to harmful substances. Work supported vulnerable individuals through direct care, clinician and community training, and policy reform across sectors including healthcare, the military and prisons. Research also played a key role in shaping public understanding and governmental and institutional practices to reduce stigma and improve mental health outcomes.

The case studies in this topic encompass the optimisation of the medication lifecycle, from development of drug dosing strategies, to prescribing frameworks and policy, and provision to patients. Studies may consider ares of benefit-risk ratios, population diversity, reduction of prescribing errors, as well as access and adherence to treatments, and service provision to particular patient groups.

Case studies in this topic contain research pertaining to greenhouse gas emissions, atmosphere and climate. The studies discuss climate change mitigation through improved greenhouse gas measurement, refined emissions reporting, and the development of decision support tools. They include research validating CO₂ emissions, accounting for methane and hydrocarbon impacts, and shaping global and national policies—including UK Net Zero targets, the UN Paris Agreement, and the Montreal Protocol. Advances also focus on satellite observations, carbon capture and storage (including negative emissions and cryogenic methods), emissions reduction in agriculture, shipping and aviation, and the environmental benefits of novel technologies such as aerosol valves and the CarbFix system.

Case studies in this topic address respiratory health, including asthma, allergies and respiratory diseases. Research covers drug development and therapies, treatments and disease management, as well as prevention and care. Studies in this topic often discuss best clinical practice, therapy development, healthcare delivery and service provision, and healthcare policy. Studies in this topic also extend to respiratory conditions such as breathlessness and sleep apnoea.

This research addresses HIV prevention and treatment, and sexual health. Research encompasses clinical practice, public health policy, prevention, and community interventions, as well as scientific developments, diagnostic tools, and therapies to reduce HIV transmission and improve treatment outcomes. Frequent themes include healthcare access and equity, community engagement, and public health policies. Sexual health, relationships and education studies are also incorporated in this topic.

Research in this topic has transformed how scientific knowledge is produced, shared, and accessed. Case studies informed national and international open access policies, strengthened GDPR-compliant data practices, and improved editorial standards and transparency across scientific publishing. Projects advanced open, scholar-led, and experimental publishing models and worked with libraries and publishers to broaden public access to research. Researchers developed influential open databases—from genetics to socio-economic data—as well as open-source tools and data ressources for digital humanities and open research software abroad many scientific fields. Citizen science initiatives empowered public participation in data collection, while efforts in knowledge organization and publishing reform shaped the future of accessible, ethical, and high-quality research dissemination.

topic_name_long: Public Services, Civil Service & Local Governance
description: Research in this topic has strengthened the design, delivery, and governance of public services, and local government. Projects informed evidence-based policymaking and evaluation, supported public service reform, and improved civil service workforce training, communication and strategy. Researchers developed outcome-focused models for service innovation and helped local authorities adopt peer-led improvement approaches. Case studies enhanced both local and national procurement practices, supported small business participation in local decision-making, and shaped reforms to civil service workforce planning. Work also guided local government initiatives and revenue generation, simplified public administration across sectors, and reduced corruption—promoting more transparent, accountable, and effective governance across the UK.

This topic covers marine and aquatic research with case studies examining environmental conservation, sustainable management, and protection strategies for aquaculture, fisheries and marine environments. Studies include aspects of statistical analysis, species conservation, aquaculture development, fisheries regulation, biodiversity assessment, and marine planning approaches. Key themes are environmental protection, strengthened policy development, and improved sustainability. Some coastal management, and community engagement research is also incorporated.

This topic focuses on telecommunications with case studies covering network technologies, wireless systems, and connectivity solutions. Research encompasses 5G development, wireless communication protocols, optical fiber technologies, internet infrastructure improvements, and 'Inernet of Things' connectivity systems. Case studies may demonstrate enhanced network performance, improved communication standards, or commercial innovations across telecommunications policy, infrastructure development, and digital service delivery.

topic_name_long: Occupational, Transport & Fire Safety & Emergency Responses
description: This portfolio of research addresses critical challenges in occupational, transport, and fire safety, as well as emergency preparedness and response. It demonstrates how academic expertise has influenced legislation, policy, design, training, and technological innovation to protect lives, improve public safety, and enhance emergency response systems across sectors.Key impacts include: improving fire safety engineering through advanced computer modelling and smoke toxicity assessments; shaping emergency response protocols for spontaneous volunteers; informing evacuation and blast safety strategies; reducing risks in hazardous occupations through behavioural science and materials research; and enhancing road safety through innovations in driver training, vehicle technology (e.g., Intelligent Speed Assistance), and road safety improvements based on AI collision modelling. The research has also led to more targeted fire prevention through novel informatics, and improved public safety policies.Through interdisciplinary methods—spanning engineering, psychology, data science, and policy research—this work has strengthened safety and resilience frameworks and technology both in the UK and internationally.

This body of research addresses poverty alleviation, social mobility, and international development, influencing how governments, NGOs, and international bodies design, implement, and evaluate policies aimed at improving the lives of marginalised populations.Internationally, the work has transformed approaches to poverty measurement and financial aid effectiveness, informed major anti-poverty initiatives—including programmes targeting the ultra-poor and international microfinance schemes—and shaped global frameworks such as the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. It has empowered marginalised voices in economic governance, enhanced land rights for women, and informed humanitarian responses in complex political economies such as South Sudan. Innovative interdisciplinary approaches, including evolutionary anthropology, have also advanced development policy and influenced fields from agricultural policy to reproductive health.In the UK, the research in this cluster focused on poverty, often seeking ways to reduce child povertyand ensure mobility, including direct influence on relevant legislation. Across all contexts, the work supports co-produced, equitable governance and evidence-led policy to tackle poverty and promote inclusive, sustainable development.

This topic focuses on pollinator with case studies researching protection strategies, policy and regulatory frameworks, and land management practices. Research encompasses pollinator protection measures, pesticide control policies, biodiversity support initiatives, and evidence-based intervention development.

This topic encompasses a wide range of research aimed at improving employment conditions, labour standards, and wage policy. Case studies focus on reducing wage inequality, supporting low-paid and precarious workers, and promoting inclusive labour markets, but also focus on labour market efficiency and ensuring high employment rates. Research has informed minimum wage legislation and pay-setting bodies in the UK and internationally, encouraged adoption of the Living Wage, and contributed to reforms in unemployment and employment policies. Other work has advanced understanding of occupational regulation, Universal Basic Income, and digital transformation of work. Studies have also adviced on trade unions and their role in the political economy, promoted decent work principles through international institutions, and improved employability programmes for disadvantaged groups. Workplace well-being, and the rights of ageing and migrant workers are further particular labour market aspects that the research advised on.

Case studies in this topic cover dental and oral health, including research into product development, prevention and treatment of dental diseases, child healthcare, and service provision improvements. Common themes include improved clinical outcomes, reduced health inequalities, policy improvements and service provision improvements.

topic_name_long: Gender, Race & Class Equity at Work
description: This topic brings together research focused on advancing workplace equity across dimensions of gender, race, class, sexuality, and belief. Case studies explore the drivers of the gender pay gap and support organisations in embedding change through pay analysis, positive action, and taking into account female lifecourses from childbearing to menopause. Research has influenced board-level gender diversity in UK companies, shaped women’s enterprise and entrepreneurship policy, and informed strategies for career progression among minority ethnic professionals. Work has also tackled barriers to social mobility in elite professions and the creative industries, improved workplace experiences for LGBTQ+ employees, and supported policy development to prevent discrimination based on religion or belief.

Case studies in this topic focus on Ireland’s history, culture, and political landscape, with emphasis on reshaping entrenched socio-political narratives to drive reconciliation and foster a shared sense of history and identity. Research informs policy, education, and practical initiatives aimed at promoting collaboration, peacebuilding, political engagement, economic development, and cultural vitality within conflicted and/or marginalised communities. Many case studies use arts and history to address the complexities of Northern Ireland’s historic and contemporary sectarianism, helping to bridge community divides through commemoration, reconciliation and justice, particularly for those affected by conflict and marginalisation.

Case studies in this topic cover research into treatments and rehabilitation across orthopaedics, biomechanics and kinesiology practice. Studies include areas such as joint replacement procedures, trauma management, rehabilitation services, biomechanical analysis, prosthetic development. Case studies demonstrate improvements in patient outcomes, healthcare cost reduction, and clinical practice guidelines and policy.

This topic encompasses agricultural plant research across disease management strategies, crop improvement technologies, and food security solutions. Case studies cover plant disease epidemiology, crop breeding techniques, pest management approaches, genetic modifications, sustainable farming practices, environmental protection strategies, and biotechnology applications. Case studies often demonstrate policy influence, agricultural productivity enhancements, and environmentally sustainable crop protection across global food production systems.

Research in this topic highlighted and enabled the crucial role of translation and multilingual communication in global collaboration, diplomacy and cultural exchange. Case studies supported the training, support and professionalisation of translators across diverse international contexts. Work celebrated multilingual engagement in literature and performance, using translation as a tool for preserving and sharing heritage, fostering cross-cultural understanding and promoting inclusive, multicultural interaction.

This topic focuses on geology, fossil fuels and mining research, including policy development, extraction technologies, environmental protection measures, and resource management strategies across oil, gas, and mineral industries. The research encompasses studies on hydrocarbon reservoir management, geological exploration methods, mining techniques, as well as environmental impact mitigation, decommissioning strategies, safety protocols, digital analysis tools, and mathematical modeling approaches. Case studies often consider regulatory frameworks, industrial efficiency improvements, and sustainable resource extraction practices for energy and mining operations.

topic_name_long: International Law, Human Rights, Indigenous & Environmental Justice
description: Case studies in this topic inform the protection and enforcement of human rights and international legislation across a range of global contexts, including prisons, conflict and post-conflict zones, border, and authoritarian regimes. Collaborating with NGOs, governments, policy groups, and communities, this work contributes to reforming justice systems and establishing legal presidents, making human rights more universally definable, enforceable and recognised. The research informed conflict resolution, international law, and legal accountability for human rights violations, while raising awareness of the experience of persecuted groups, victims on historical and ongoing abuses, and those working to defend human rights. There is also a key focus in advocating for indigenous rights and environmental justice, supporting self-representation, land rights, and sustainable access to resources.

This topic addresses nuclear science, engineering, and policy research and their translation into safety standards, regulatory frameworks, and operational improvements across the nuclear sector. The research encompasses studies on reactor safety, materials, radioactive waste management, as well as radiation protection, decommissioning strategies, risk assessment, software, and modeling tools. Some case studies also consider tools for facilitating conversation and awareness in the nuclear sector.

Case studies in this topic advance understandings of mental health and promote the development of sustainable, patient-centred support systems across a range of settings. Research informed policy and practices in institutions such as government, healthcare, the military, education, and social services, foregrounding mental health and wellbeing as essential aspects of public health. Many highlight the needs of underserved or misunderstood groups, particularly in low-resources or culturally specific contexts for more informed, resilient and inclusive mental health provisions. Strong emphasis is placed on developing understandings of the relationship between mental health and media. There is particular emphasis on the role of media in shaping body image, eating disorders and mental wellbeing in young people and women, as well as safeguarding against digital addiction and social media ‘echo chambers’.

Case studies in this topic address the complex relationships between food, diet and health across a range of contexts. Research in this topic informed NGOs, governments and the food industry on issues such as food marketing, insecurity, accessibility and sustainability. Work supports the fostering of healthy eating habits and contributes scientific understanding of diet-related diseases and development of interventions to reduce their impact. A number of case studies focus on education and early-life intervention, influencing school-based policies and lifelong health education to promote informed, sustainable dietary habits from an early age.

Case studies in this topic worked to preserve Welsh and Gaelic languages and promote their learning to safeguard and broaden current and future usage. Several provided practical means by collating and improving access to resources such as dictionaries and online databases. Case studies also worked to recognise and improve language diversity, recognising the social and economic benefits of such multilingualism. This included introducing their official use in more settings, such as schools, workplaces and courts of law. Many underpinned governmental policies to support their acquisition and wider use. This was largely seen in language teaching in schools and online classes enabled by case studies providing resource access, teacher training and development of curricula. Addressing ‘linguistic fragility’ in native-speaking communities reconnected with heritage and supported rich cultural partnerships that fostered a strong sense of community and identity on local, regional and national scales.

This topic addresses reasearch into healthcare ethics and health data governance and their translation into policy frameworks, regulatory standards, and clinical practice guidelines. The research encompasses studies on patient privacy and data protection, clinical research governance, end-of-life care ethics, as well as digital security methods, anonymization frameworks, and ethical decision-making tools. Case studies often demonstrate how ethical research influences healthcare policy, regulatory approval processes, and professional practice standards. The topic includes examples of successful ethics-to-policy translation that improve patient safety, data security, and ethical standards across healthcare systems.

This topic addresses software engineering, hardware development, and digital technologies research and their translation into commercial products, industrial applications, and societal benefits. The research encompasses studies on software verification, embedded systems, semiconductor design, as well as open-source development tools, formal modeling approaches, and digital platform technologies. Case studies often discuss product development, industry standards, and technological innovation across a vast range of applications. The topic includes examples of successful technology transfer including new start-up companies, open-source software adoption, hardware optimization, and digital solutions that improve efficiency, reliability, and accessibility across multiple sectors.

This topic brings together research that has shaped the design, regulation, and integrity of democratic processes in the UK and internationally. Case studies address the mechanics of democracy—from electoral system design and boundary reform to the regulation of campaign finance and polling practices. Contributions include improving election polling methodologies and informing public understanding of polling accuracy, as well as shaping electoral policy, such as campaign regulation. Internationally, research has informed electoral integrity efforts, supported peaceful transfers of power, and improved democratic oversight through legislative reform and election monitoring. These impacts have strengthened public confidence in democratic institutions and enhanced the fairness and functionality of electoral systems.

This topic addresses air pollution research and its translation into policy, regulation, and technological solutions to protect public health and environmental quality. The research encompasses studies on the health impacts of both outdoor and indoor air pollution, as well as sampling/sensing technologies, statistical modeling approaches and air quality data are included. Case studies often demonstrate how scientific evidence influences policy interventions and applications extend across public health policy, environmental regulation, urban planning, industrial compliance, climate change mitigation, and technological innovation in air quality monitoring and pollution control systems.

This topic considers the area of veterinary science and animal welfare, covering companion animal health, livestock management, and wildlife conservation. Development of improved diagnostic tools, treatment methods, and welfare assessment techniques is a large component of this topic. This topic includes case studies that demonstrate advances in disease prevention, vaccine development, genetic testing, and surveillance systems that improve animal health outcomes, as well as welfare standards through housing improvements, pain assessment tools, and evidence-based management practices across domestic, farm, and laboratory animals. Applications span across veterinary medicine, agricultural production, food safety, policy development, and conservation amongst others.

This topic considers the treatment and prevention of breast cancer, ovarian cancer, and their related conditions. Development of improved therapeutic approaches, diagnostic tools, and personalized treatment strategies is a large component of this topic. Case studies for improved patient outcomes include improved treatments through risk assessment tools, radiotherapy innovations, and patient-centered care approaches, as well as cancer prevention strategies, therapy optimisations, surgical techniques, and supportive care. Initiatives often focus on clinical implementation and evidence-based decision-making to improve survival rates and quality of life for cancer patients.

This topic considers the area of meteorological and climate science, covering weather forecasting, climate modeling, and atmospheric research. Development of improved prediction systems and observational technologies is a large component of this topic. Case studies demonstrate advances in forecasting accuracy and extreme weather attribution that improve public safety and economic outcomes, as well as climate resilience through satellite data analysis, risk assessment, and automated prediction systems. Applications are broad and span across aviation safety, urban planning, disaster risk reduction, insurance analysis, and international development amongst others. The topic also includes initiatives focused on technology transfer and capacity building to promote climate adaptation and societal resilience.

This topic focuses on high-performance computing, data analytics, and distributed systems applications across business, scientific research, and public sectors. It encompasses supercomputing, cloud platforms, big data processing, and data governance for improved computational efficiency and decision-making. Some studies demonstrating industrial transformation including manufacturing optimization, financial services, and public sector digitalization are incorporated. Case studies also cover computational infrastructure, data science methodologies, and associated security considerations. Key themes include system scalability, algorithmic optimization, and commercial applications across finance, healthcare, manufacturing, and defense.

This topic showcases case studies addressing the representation, rights and experiences of LGBTQ+ communities across a range of social, legal and cultural contexts. Research in this topic informed legal frameworks, policy and institutional practices to improve understanding of diverse sexual and gender identities and provide better protection against discrimination and hate crime. Areas of focus include cultural heritage and visibility, mental health and wellbeing, and LGBTQ+ experiences in institutions such as the police, military, education and government. Case studies also explore issues in areas such as adoption, marital law, and asylum, working to advance equity, representation and social justice for LGBTQ+ communities.

topic_name_long: Military: Personnel, Ethics, Equipment, Strategy & Intelligence
description: This topic showcases research that has strengthened military effectiveness, ethics, and support systems across defence institutions in the UK and internationally. Case studies span improvements to personnel performance and wellbeing—including training protocols, equipment upgrades, and digital support services for veterans and families—as well as research that shaped ethical frameworks for military decision-making, drone operation, and cultural property protection. Strategic insights informed UK foreign and defence policy, enhanced defence intelligence tradecraft, and contributed to doctrine development and preparedness. Other work supported transparency in biodefence, improved weapons acquisition practices, and shaped regulation of emerging technologies such as autonomous weapons systems.

Case studies in this topic explore the representation, rights and heritage of Islamic communities, particularly within the UK. Research shaped how Islamic communities, and the Middle East more broadly, are understood in British culture and governance. It supports efforts to combat Islamophobia through clearer definitions and improved policing practices, both online and offline. Many case studies focused on fostering cross-cultural and interfaith dialogue through collaborative outreach, education, and cultural exhibitions, involving schools, councils, law enforcement, and faith communities. They also highlighted the cultural contributions of Islamic communities, promoting recognition, inclusion and social cohesion in historically divided contexts.

This topic highlights research that has significantly enhanced the collection, analysis, and application of economic, demographic, and policy-relevant data. Case studies include improvements to numerous population censuses, mortality estimates, and life tables; the development of more accurate measures of income inequality and economic performance; and novel modelling of international development metrics. Research also shaped official statistics used by the UK Office for National Statistics and other national and international agencies. It provided important methods improvements for official statistics, e.g. better geospatial methods for boundary design as well as improved data visualisation and communication. Work in this area underpinned policymaking in fields ranging from pensions and insurance to tourism and regional governance.

This topic brings together research that has shaped emergency medical care, ambulance services with those focussed on disaster response at national and international levels. It includes innovations in pre-hospital care to better patient outcomes, improved triage systems, and improvements to ambulancing in emergency as well as analysis to reduce unnecessary hospital transfers. Work in this area also addressed systemic challenges like emergency department overcrowding and improved health outcomes through bettering community response and medical device access for medical emergencies. Beyond medical emergencies, research has influenced disaster preparedness and response strategies globally—enhancing community resilience, informing financial strategies for disaster recovery, and shaping UN and Red Cross policies as well as governmental, corporate and volunteer efforts to protect and support populations in crisis contexts.

This topic brings together research that has informed and reshaped international relations, diplomacy, and foreign policy in complex and contested global contexts. It encompasses work on the strategic use of soft power, religious engagement; on border relations and identity politics as factors in regional stability; and on historical narratives that shape modern political alignments. Research has influenced UK and international policy on regions including the Balkans, East Asia, the Arab world, and even the polar zones, while also advising on constructive diplomatic engagement in both adversarial and friendly contexts. Other work has helped broker international agreements, guided policy on maritime and border security, and informed the rights and political situation of stateless populations. Across these contributions, a shared focus lies in supporting peaceful cooperation, cross-cultural understanding, and evidence-based foreign policy.

This topic brings together research that has shaped how workplaces promote wellbeing, manage risks, and organise work. A key focus is improving mental health, emotional resilience, and job quality through changes to HR policies, health and safety practices, and support systems across sectors—from policing and law to gig economy platforms. Case studies explore how organisations address workplace conflict, bullying, and stress; how they embed ethical practices; and how work design influences both productivity and employee wellbeing. Research has also guided public bodies and trade unions in reforming employment relations, modernising management structures, and promoting fair and decent work. At its core, this topic reflects a commitment to creating more humane, effective, and sustainable workplaces through evidence-based policy and practice.

This topic addresses vehicle engineering and includes case studies across modelling, analysis and design of vehicles and their components. Case studies are often concerned with improving sustainability of vehicle manufacture and operation, reducing emissions and improving efficiency. Further considerations are developments in safety, maintenance requirements, performance and reliability. Some works also consider vehicle care, maintenance and preservation.

topic_name_long: Virtual Reality, Video Games, Creative Digital Industries
description: This topic focuses on immersive technologies (VR/AR) and Human-Computer Interaction applications across healthcare, manufacturing, education, and entertainment. It encompasses user experience design, industry collaboration, and research translation for improved business processes and creative economy development. Case studies cover immersive technologies, digital innovation, and academia-business collaboration. Key themes include user experience design, accessibility, economic impact, and applications in gaming, healthcare, education, and cultural sectors. Public engagement and industry transformation through knowledge transfer are also incorporated.

Research in this topic address the understanding, diagnosis, treatment and prevention of metabolic diseases and obesity. Case studies informed national and global public health policy, improving risk assessment and shaping preventative strategies. Work shaped governmental, health institutional and public understandings of these diseases and factors underpinning. New medical approaches enhanced treatment effectiveness and patient outcomes. Public health initiatives promoted health literacy and lifelong behavioural change from childhood through adulthood, reducing risk factors.

Case studies in this topic aimed to deepen public engagement with environmental issues and inform policy for the protection of the environment through artist and cultural production, exhibition and collaboration. Research highlighted the cultural, social, economic and health value of nature, landscapes, and ecology, promoting sustainable change, environmental awareness, advocacy, and activism.

This topic showcases how research has influenced the development of social enterprises and transformed entrepreneurship education globally. Impact includes support for small businesses and social ventures in embedding sustainability and social responsibility into their practices, often in alignment with the international development goals. Case studies highlight new models for social innovation and co-operative practice, support structures for entrepreneurship in justice and fair trade contexts, and practical tools for inclusive enterprise development in Africa and Latin America. In parallel, research has shaped entrepreneurship education across multiple sectors and continents, from developing creative pedagogies to inspiring entrepreneurial thinking among scientists, students, and youth. Together, these case studies demonstrate how entrepreneurial capacity can be built to generate both economic and social value.

This topic focuses on pharmaceutical research and biotechnology innovation to advance drug discovery, diagnostics, and therapeutic development. Case studies show development of treatments, therapies, and drug delivery systems that improve patient outcomes. Case studies also cover enhanced diagnostic capabilities through point-of-care testing, biomarker identification, and advanced screening technologies. The topic also incorporates novel scientific methods for protein engineering, synthetic biology, and computational drug design, leading to faster and more cost-effective pharmaceutical development. Initiatives are often focused on commercialisation and technology transfer, particularly through spin-out companies and industry partnerships, to promote therapeutic innovation and economic growth in the life sciences sector.

This topic contains case studies describing developments in the treatment and care of corectal cancers. This incorporates screening, diagnostics, surveillance, prevention, and adjuvant care, generally resulting in improved patient outcomes and/or reduced treatment costs. Case studies often detail impacts in clinical trials, as well as updates to guidelines and policy for corectal cancer.

In this topic research relating to volcanology and seismology is collated, with case studies primarily covering aspects of monitoring, modelling & prediction of events, as well as prevention and disaster response. This includes studies into public health, monitoring and sensing, and development of technologies for this. Broadly; increasing safety, public wellbeing and reducing disruption are key themes of the topic.

This topic focuses on healthcare professionals (HCPs) and management of the healthcare workforce and services.
